To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) effect sizes vary across different types of studies and research areas, with some studies having large effects and other studies having small effects; (2) researchers should report effect sizes in their research reports, and (3) researchers should interpret effect sizes in the context of prior research in the same or related research areas.

(a) researchers can estimate and interpret effect size statistics for a variety of study designs and (b) effect sizes can be interpreted by directly comparing them with effect sizes in the prior related research literature.

(a) the majority of studies in the literature on the effects of the use of alcohol on aggression report significant positive effects, and (b) the effect size estimates of the alcohol aggression relationship in this literature range from 0.10 to 0.50.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new and efficient numerical methods for the analysis of data.
the development of a method of estimating the effects of various factors on the performance of a system.
the development of new methods for the analysis and interpretation of data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the new study’s effect size was larger than the prior related literature’s effect sizes, and thus, the results of the new study are more likely to be replicable than the prior related studies’ results.
“the present results replicated the prior literature in this area, and the present study’s effect was larger than the effect reported in study X, Y, and Z.”
“the present study provides further replication of the effect reported in the prior literature, and the effect size in the present study is similar to those in the prior literature.”
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
effect sizes are a critical component of the research report and are necessary for the evaluation of the replicability and importance of results.
we have developed a set of tools to help researchers estimate and interpret effect size statistics, and to help them compare their results with those reported in prior studies.
the authors have provided an excellent overview of the various effect sizes that are available to researchers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interpretation of effect size statistics should be guided by the question of interest and the context of the research.
the effect size statistic should always be interpreted in light of the research questions, study design, and prior related studies.
effect sizes can be used to estimate the magnitude of effects and to evaluate replicability of results.
